summary.text: Peggy Flanagan is the Democratic (DFL) nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat and has been Minnesota's lieutenant governor since 2019. A citizen of the White Earth Nation, she served on the Minneapolis school board, worked as a trainer and nonprofit leader, and served in the Minnesota House before being elected lieutenant governor on the ticket with Tim Walz. She won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over U.S. Rep. Angie Craig, 58.9% to 39.5%, and is running on health care, child care and economic-fairness proposals.

paragraphs.text: Flanagan was raised by a single mother in St. Louis Park, Minnesota, and her campaign says her family relied on Section 8 housing, SNAP and child care assistance to get by.
She is Ojibwe and a member of the White Earth Nation, and she earned a bachelor's degree in American Indian studies and child psychology from the University of Minnesota in 2002.
Flanagan was elected to the Minneapolis school board at 25, becoming its youngest member, and served from 2005 to 2009 and again in 2010.

She went on to work as a trainer for Wellstone Action, a nonprofit that trained activists, and became executive director of the Children's Defense Fund-Minnesota, where she co-chaired the Raise the Wage Coalition.
She was also a partner at The Management Center, an executive coaching firm.

In 2015 Flanagan was elected to the Minnesota House of Representatives from District 46A, a seat she held until 2019, and served on the Health and Human Services Reform, Rules and Legislative Administration, and State Government committees in the 2017 session.
She helped form the House's People of Color and Indigenous Caucus and, during the 2017-18 session, was one of two DFL members to chief-author a bill that became law.

She became lieutenant governor in 2019 as Walz's running mate, and her campaign credits her with helping pass Minnesota's paid family and medical leave program; KEYC reports she helped establish the state's Missing and Murdered Indigenous Relatives Office.
Flanagan announced her Senate campaign on February 13, 2025, after Sen. Tina Smith said she would not seek re-election.
She lives in St. Louis Park with her husband and daughter.
